{"Patient Age": 36, "Patient Sex": "Female", "Imaging Setting": "Outpatient", "Imaging Type": "CT Abdomen & Pelvis, Enhanced", "Radiology Report": "Basic Text SR Document Study: CT ABDOMEN + PELVIS AUGMENTED=AB (#1090641) Manufacturer: AGFA Completion Flag: COMPLETE Verification Flag: VERIFIED Content Date/Time: 2019-09-16 00:00:00 Diagnostic Imaging Report Current Procedure Description CT ABDOMEN + PELVIS AUGMENTED Findings Alberta Health Services Name: Brooks Health Centre DOB: Age: 36 / F ULI: Brooks, AB Phone: Unit Number: Location: Account Number: Room: Ordering Provider: DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING ***Signed*** __________________________________________________________________________________________ PROCEDURE DATE(S) : 16-SEP-2019 PROCEDURE NAME(S): CT ABDOMEN + PELVIS AUGMENTED HISTORY: GENERALIZED ABD LYMPHADENOPATHY ?ABDOMINAL PATHOLOGY CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS INDICATION: Generalized abdominal lymphadenopathy. ?Abdominal pathology TECHNIQUE: Enhanced imaging of the abdomen and pelvis was performed, with multiplanar reformats provided. Positive oral contrast was administered. COMPARISON: none available FINDINGS: The lung bases are clear. The liver is normal in size, contour and density. No worrisome solid hepatic lesions. Mild focal fatty infiltration adjacent the falciform ligament. A few cysts are scattered throughout the liver, the largest of which is in segment IVb and measures 9 mm maximally. Gallbladder appears normal. Intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary ductal system are non-dilated. Pancreatic parenchyma appears within normal limits. There are no focal pancreatic masses and there is no pancreatic ductal dilatation. Spleen is normal in size and appearance. There are no focal splenic lesions. Both adrenal glands appear normal. No evidence of a solid renal mass, nephroureterolithiasis or hydroureteronephrosis in the urinary system. Bladder is incompletely distended but grossly unremarkable. Uterus and ovaries appear grossly normal. Tubal ligation clips are present, with right tubal ligation clips within the pelvis, and left tubal ligation clip having migrated to the left mid abdomen, abutting the rectus abdominis muscle. The stomach and duodenum appear normal. Proximal small bowel appears normal. Distal small bowel is notable for mild circumferential bowel wall thickening that extends into the cecum. Haustra on the cecum are mildly thickened in a fairly diffuse manner. There are multiple small lymph nodes scattered throughout the right lower quadrant, as well as a small amount of regional inflammatory change. The largest lymph node measures 11 mm in short axis. No necrotic lymph nodes. Appendix is visualized in the right lower quadrant, extending into the deep pelvis. The proximal appendix is normal in caliber, however, the distal appendix is fluid filled and distended up to 12 mm in short axis. There is no fluid collection adjacent the appendix tip that might suggest a perforation or periappendiceal abscess. The appendix does not appear to be the center of the inflammatory change in the right lower quadrant. The large bowel does not demonstrate evidence of focal mass like thickening, stricture or obstruction. No diverticular disease or findings for acute diverticulitis. Sigmoid colon is prominently redundant. There is no significant atheromatous disease of the aorta, without aneurysm dilatation. There are numerous small lymph nodes scattered along the paraaortic margins and in the small bowel mesentery, none of these are enlarged by size criteria. No ascites. Pelvic girdle is intact. No acute fractures or aggressive lesions in the visualized thoracolumbar spine. IMPRESSION: Mild ileocecal inflammation associated with numerous lymph nodes in the right lower quadrant. Shotty lymph nodes throughout the abdominal cavity as well. Taken together, the findings are non-specific but could indicate an inflammatory bowel process such as Crohn's disease. Differential diagnosis would be an infectious/inflammatory ileitis. The appendix is mildly distended along its tip, however, it is not the center of the inflammatory process in the right lower quadrant and therefore the findings are not favored to represent a primary appendicitis. Correlate clinically in this regard for a typical history for appendicitis. Given the absence of general lymph node enlargement, lymphoma would be unlikely. Dictation Date: 16-SEP-2019 1512 by: Transcription Date: 16-SEP-2019 1529 by: Electronically Signed: 16-SEP-2019 1653 by: __________________________________________________________________________________________ Order and Accession Number(s): CT/CT ABDOMEN + PELVIS AUGMENTED CC: This page was generated from a DICOM Structured Reporting document by OFFIS DCMTK 3.6.5."}
